building.name: International Building Code with Louisiana amendments (Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code, LAC 17:I.103), enforced in New Orleans with the city's own amendments (New Orleans Code of Ordinances, Chapter 26, Section 26-14 and following)
building.edition: 2021 (the edition the state rule sets; the city's page names no edition and the city ordinance could not be opened)
building.local_amendments_note: The city's page says its amendments are 'jurisdiction-specific addenda to the International construction codes' and links to Section 26-14 on Municode, which returned 403. Only the amended Section 105.2 (work exempt from permit) was read, as reproduced on city pages. Louisiana's rule does not adopt Chapter 1 (Administration) of the model code, which is where 105.2 sits; state law bars local changes to the mandatory technical provisions (state pack, La. R.S. as printed in the commission's blue book).

permit.exempt_list_quote: 105.2 Work Exempt from Permit. Exemptions from permit requirements of this Code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this Code or any other laws or ordinances of the City of New Orleans including Vieux Carré Commission and Historic District Landmarks Commission requirements. A building permit shall not be required for the following, unless in the opinion of the Director it involves hazardous or complex conditions which require permitting and inspection: Less than 50% per exterior wall removal and replacement of deteriorated weather boards, aluminum, or vinyl siding. [...] Removal and replacement of deteriorated floorboards. Removal and replacement of unenclosed and uncovered deteriorated porches and steps that are five feet or less in height above grade [...] Interior painting, papering and similar finish work. Paving of yard when in compliance with the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance. Retaining walls which are not over three ft. in height. Exterior painting when not requiring protective scaffolding over public property or lead-based paint removal. Repairs to stucco when not requiring protective scaffolding over public property. Replacement of less than 50% of the roofing and/or gutter work with respect to one and two family dwellings. Fences up to seven ft. in height, when in compliance with the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance. Masonry walls up to three ft. in height from grade or structure, when used as a fence and when in compliance with the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance. Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached one- and two-family dwellings. Tents with an area less than 150 sq. ft. and not located in a Fire District [...] Uncovered decks, when part of a residential use, that do not exceed 200 sq. ft. in area and thirty in. high from grade at any point, that are not attached to a dwelling unit, and that do not serve as an exit door. Replacement of cabinets and countertops when it does not also include replacement of plumbing fixtures or any fixed equipment. The above exemptions supersede the exemptions listed in the unamended Code and are in addition to any works listed as exempt in the IRC or IBC, unless deemed applicable by the Department of Safety and Permits.
permit.note: The list is the city's amended Section 105.2. It exempts 'Interior painting, papering and similar finish work' and 'Replacement of cabinets and countertops when it does not also include replacement of plumbing fixtures or any fixed equipment'; toilet partitions are not named. The same list on the Historic District Landmarks Commission's handout (undated, issued under Mayor Cantrell) lacks the cabinets item. The city's non-structural renovation permit page says that permit 'is required for any construction or changes of use within an existing building (interior or exterior)'.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to New Orleans job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Gulf Coast humidity and see the local rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for New Orleans hotels, restaurants, schools and port warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Louisiana's rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and state law has every city and parish enforce them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.code_change_bullet: - **New rules on January 1, 2027:** Louisiana has scheduled newer editions of its building and plumbing rules to take effect that day. Ask the New Orleans Department of Safety and Permits which edition applies to your project.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** New Orleans requires a renovation permit for construction inside an existing building unless the work is on its exempt list. The list covers interior painting, papering and similar finish work, and replacing cabinets and countertops, and doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask the Building Division at the New Orleans Department of Safety and Permits (504-658-7130) whether your replacement needs one. Plumbing permits come from the Sewerage and Water Board, not the city. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the New Orleans Department of Safety and Permits
page.install_rule: New Orleans licenses electrical and mechanical contractors itself. For other construction work the city points to the Louisiana State Licensing Board for Contractors, and a permit application asks for the contractor's license information. Louisiana requires a state commercial contractor license for commercial projects of $50,000 or more, labor and materials included, so smaller jobs fall below the state requirement. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: On a commercial project of $50,000 or more, the contractor needs a Louisiana state license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Louisiana has no state wage law for public construction, so a required wage applies only on federally funded jobs, at the rate the U.S. Department of Labor sets for the parish. For a carpenter on building work in Orleans Parish that is $19.37 an hour plus $2.46 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 10% in New Orleans: 5% state and 5% Orleans Parish. Three small districts add their own tax: 0.245% in the French Quarter district, 1% at Magnolia Marketplace and 2% at Riverwalk-Spanish Plaza.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels and convention venues:** finishes that match the property in guest-facing restrooms, HDPE or phenolic where crowds and nightly washdown are hard on stalls.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (ADA-ABA Accessibility Guidelines), enforced by the Louisiana Office of State Fire Marshal; Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code: International Building Code, 2021 Edition, with Louisiana amendments (LAC 17:I.103) and International Plumbing Code, 2021 Edition, with Louisiana amendments (LAC 17:I.111), in force since January 1, 2023, with the 2024 editions scheduled for January 1, 2027; New Orleans Code of Ordinances, Chapter 26, Section 26-14 and following (the city's amendments to the International Building Code, including Section 105.2, work exempt from permit); Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans Plumbing Code; NFPA 286 for HDPE under the International Building Code.
